behavior: deleteChat requests shortcut deletion UI by setting D=shortcut. enabled is isChatConversation&&!ae&&!isDeleting, with ae=G(pa,serverConversationId) retained as an opaque source predicate; isActive delegates bas. Deletion ownership predicate rejects null/temporary conversations; absent owner is allowed, otherwise owner user_id must match the selected user identifier, with optional split at __. Effective input identity is unobserved.

Account deletion delegates safeDelete /conversation/id/{conversation_id}; the specific 404 conversation_deleted is accepted. behavior: Local markThreadUnread requires the current local-thread route conversation to match and Bn.canMarkUnread. Its callback rechecks non-null ID and supplies conversationId/hostId to Jda.markThreadAsUnread. This is not the account tm registration guard.

Jda.markThreadAsUnread delegates the selected manager when sF.canMarkUnread is not exactly false. It neither returns nor awaits/catches that manager call in this function. copyConversationMarkdown delegates qda with scope and intl without returning its completion.

Account tm registers markThreadUnread without a selected options object; its callback delegates jFr and catches rejection to an account-conversation error toast. The saved f_ caller omits tm in temporary or archived-preview views; full mode/mount closure remains open.
jFr awaits MFr with status mT.UNREAD. It is an account-status adapter, not the local manager call.

MFr uses a local Hk path for missing server ID or tpp origins. It guards incompatible async status, captures host/account, sets a scoped pending object and queues a guarded async-status POST; post-response updates require the captured identity still current. finally removes only the same pending object.
sF is the source-scoped derived unread eligibility facade that delegates a9n. Its name alone does not establish canMarkUnread or physical persistence.

a9n combines the primary unread root, fallback/legacy unread root and unread side-conversation IDs, then delegates i9n. Effective root/provider values and the complete i9n policy remain a qualified external predicate.
clearAllUnreads reads Rcc: truthy calls Mcc directly, otherwise requests a Fcc dialog via bf. The selected registration supplies no enabled options.
Rcc requests keyed preference skip-clear-all-unreads-confirmation with default false; actual storage authority/durability remain unresolved.

On confirmation Fcc optionally sets Rcc=true when the checkbox is checked, calls Mcc without awaiting and closes immediately. Cancel only closes. This selected dialog has no operation-pending guard or rollback/error handler for the Mcc Promise.

Mcc waits for saved unread data; a null result returns. It combines local/remote targets, clears local Hk flags and delegates selected account unread entries to PFr, updates inbox item readAt/unreadRunCounts and dispatches inbox-automation-runs-mark-all-read before awaiting a0r. Only succeeded remote task IDs get the later has_unread_turn cache rewrite; task queries are invalidated and account errors may show feedback. This is not limited to visible rows and supplies no single atomic rollback.

behavior: Fe defaults enabled and canCopy to true, priority to fallback and renderMode to conversation. Registration enabled depends on enabled, not canCopy; the selector independently rejects canCopy=false or tpp/flora origins. Current rendered turns, comparison prompt and source content overrides affect the selected code block.

Pe scans turns/items newest first for assistant messages and returns the last eligible code block in the first qualifying assistant item. Content references require valid attributes/reference data and a non-streaming boundary. Ordinary code uses f6c fence state before selection, with source codeBlocks overrides preserved.

f6c tracks backtick/tilde fence marker and minimum length, supports at most three leading spaces and closes only on matching marker with a long-enough delimiter and whitespace-only suffix. It rejects a backtick opening info string containing a backtick.

Fe ignores repeated triggers during an active history load. If selected content is absent, loading requires loadHistory, a server ID, no selected blocker and history complete===false. AbortController/watch cancels on changed current conversation, node, comparison prompt or copyLastCodeBlock command state; effect cleanup aborts and finally unsubscribes/clears the matching controller. Clipboard success feedback is suppressed after abort.

behavior: Overflow openSideChat requires the workspace permission facade, an ID, neither archive flag, no restricted thread marker, a sideChatTab and no source platform blocker. Callback delegates xks with source conversation/cwd/host/collaboration and reports rejection. These conditions differ from Jt action availability.

Jt finds the side-chat action from qAs output; enabled is action!=null and isActive is the supplied callback. Command selection calls the supplied onActionSelect or Zt. surface defaults panel-launcher, target defaults right; new-tab suggestions and replaceTabId remain distinct inputs.
Xt selects exactly action.id===side-chat; action name matching is not evidence that arbitrary actions are equivalent.
The default side action selector simply returns action.onSelect(). A supplied onActionSelect may replace this behavior.
The side-chat permission facade _j requires no persistentWorkspace and routeKind other than other; it is not a constant boolean product gate.

qAs derives side-chat availability from a local-thread route, _j, archive predicates, restricted-thread predicate and platform guard, then passes actions through ejs with codexFeatureAccess/surface/target. side-chat action delegates xks and closes on fulfilled Promise, reports rejection, and preserves replacement/target arguments. Complete ejs access filtering remains delegated.

xks rechecks _j and archive predicates, creates a pending tab, requests a conversation via ZOs and installs the resulting side-chat tab. If pending tab becomes stale, it cleans up the created conversation. Missing cloud environment, setup error, durable/non-durable cleanup, replacement, retry and close cancellation have distinct paths. Tab creation does not prove task/model execution.

behavior: Gc openReviewTab requires ready state and either remote showReviewTab or a local git repository descriptor. Its callback delegates lAs; this differs from the adjacent toggleReviewTab and from reviewDelivery preference.

lAs returns false under Qp, otherwise uses the existing DIFF panel or a validated target/default right, delegates pAs with revealAndFocus=false and optionally focuses via GP. It opens/adopts Changes rather than applying the toggle behavior of the neighboring command.

pAs delegates Gj with the DIFF singleton, durable route/default state, insertion/replacement args and Changes title. Deletion ownership predicate rejects null/temporary conversations; absent owner is allowed, otherwise owner user_id must match the selected user identifier, with optional split at __. Effective input identity is unobserved.

Account deletion delegates safeDelete /conversation/id/{conversation_id}; the specific 404 conversation_deleted is accepted.
